pr.title: JumpThreading: Avoid computing dominators to identify loop headers.
pr.description:
JumpThreading tries to avoid threading through loop headers to avoid creating irreducible CFGs.

However, computing dominators is expensive, and accounts up to 20 % of the runtime of the JumpThreading pass for some cases like serde.

This PR proposes to approximate according to the post-order traversal order. We define a "maybe" loop header as a block which is visited after its predecessor in post-order.

pr.author: cjgillot

analysis.originalLogic: The pass computed exact loop headers using dominators: a block was a loop header if it dominated at least one predecessor. The old helper built `let dominators = body.basic_blocks.dominators();`, visited reachable blocks, and inserted `succ` when `dominators.dominates(succ, bb)`. The resulting set was stored as `loop_headers` and checked in `start_from_switch`, in the recursive walk ("Do not thread through loop headers."), and in the final verification assertion `assert!(to.chain.iter().all(|&block| !finder.loop_headers.contains(block)));`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The PR under test replaces the exact dominator test with a postorder heuristic: traverse `traversal::postorder(body)`, and for every successor not yet in `visited`, insert that successor into `maybe_loop_headers`; mark `bb` visited only after checking its successors. This is the historically applied transformation being studied, not an invented wrong rewrite and not a demonstrated bug. Its semantic risk is that the approximation can differ from the exact dominator definition (typically over-approximating loop headers), and ordering mistakes such as marking `bb` visited before scanning successors would miss self-loop headers `bb1: goto -> bb1;`. The patch itself states the approximation is acceptable because the pass only needs a heuristic.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR control-flow graphs processed by JumpThreading, especially reachable CFGs containing loops, nested loops, self-loops, switches, cleanup blocks, cross/back edges, and potentially irreducible CFGs. The optimization targets functions where dominator computation is a large fraction of JumpThreading runtime, as with serde-like workloads. Two programs can differ only in whether the CFG contains a cycle/self-loop versus a purely acyclic forward-edge structure, and in whether a jump-threading opportunity lies through a block classified as a loop header.
pitfalls: Marking `bb` visited before inspecting successors loses self-loop detection, because `bb -> bb` would see `bb` as already visited.
Using preorder instead of postorder would classify ordinary acyclic forward successors as maybe loop headers.
The postorder approximation can over-approximate true loop headers relative to the dominator definition, reducing threading opportunities even though it remains conservative.
The old dominator definition is itself only exact for reducible CFGs; on irreducible CFGs both old and new logic are heuristics.

The final verification assertion checks `!finder.maybe_loop_headers.contains(block)` for every block in each threading chain; a bad loop-header set can trip this assertion or permit threading through a loop header.
Do not assume the approximation is a bug fix: the patch does not establish a correctness bug in the dominator-based version.
preconditions: JumpThreading is running on a MIR `Body` and has recorded threading opportunities.
The loop-header set is consulted before starting from a switch (`start_from_switch`) and during the recursive opportunity walk.
The CFG may contain self-loops such as `bb1: goto -> bb1;`, which require checking successors before marking the current block visited.
Postorder traversal naturally covers reachable blocks; loop-header classification should be conservative to preserve the no-threading-through-loop-headers invariant.
analysis.summary: JumpThreading replaces its expensive dominator-based loop-header computation with a postorder approximation so it can still avoid threading through loop headers without paying for dominators. The PR is a performance optimization, not a confirmed bug fix, and adds no regression tests.
analysis.testStrategy: Create focused Rust MIR tests for JumpThreading that include: a self-loop (`bb1: goto -> bb1;`), a simple back edge, nested loops, a switch with a threading opportunity that would pass through a loop header, and an irreducible CFG. Compile with debug assertions enabled so the pass's final "do not thread through a loop header" assertion is checked, and compare emitted MIR between the dominator-based and postorder-approximation implementations. Also test a purely acyclic diamond/forward-edge CFG to ensure no ordinary successor is misclassified. The supplied patch contains no regression-test changes, so these tests must be added rather than inferred from the patch. No execution or reproduction is claimed here.
analysis.trigger: JumpThreading must avoid threading through loop headers so it does not create irreducible CFGs, but computing dominators is expensive and "accounts up to 20 % of the runtime of the JumpThreading pass for some cases like serde." The pass therefore needs a cheaper conservative loop-header heuristic.
